text.text: A rushed intake is the root of most failed searches. Fifteen extra minutes here saves two weeks later.
Questions to cover
Why is the role open and what happened to the last person?
What would the first ninety days look like for a great hire?
Which two skills are non-negotiable and which can be taught?
Salary range and what could move it; benefits that candidates always ask about.
Interview rounds, who is in them, and how many days between rounds.
After the call
Create the job order with salary, target fill date and level.
Write the role page: the role, search plan and interview process.
Send the employer a short summary of what you heard and ask them to correct it.
Agree these before you source
Fee and guarantee period on the employer row
A named person who gives feedback within two working days
Whether the role is exclusive to us
What goes to the employer
A short note: why this person, in three sentences.
Their resume, with any changes they approved.
Salary expectations and notice period, stated plainly.
Two lines on what they asked about the role.
What never goes
Anything the candidate asked you to keep private.
A salary figure you have not confirmed with them this week.
After you send
Log the submission with the submitted date.
Set a reminder to call the employer in two working days.
Tell the candidate what happens next and by when.
A candidate who never hears back stops answering your calls. A short update is always better than silence.
From offer to start date
When a submission reaches Offer, call both sides the same day and confirm the number.
Record the agreed pay on the submission only once the candidate has said yes.
Press Confirm placement after the written offer is signed and the start date is agreed.
Send the employer the fee invoice according to the terms on their row.
During the guarantee period
Call the new hire at day 7, day 30 and day 60.
Note anything that sounds like trouble and tell the employer early.
If a hire leaves, open a replacement job order at no new fee and link it in the notes.
Why this matters
Employers remember how replacements were handled far longer than they remember the original fee.
Agenda for forty-five minutes
Past target fill date: each job order gets a plan or a decision to close.
Interviews this week: who is prepping each candidate?
Stale candidates: anyone available who has not been contacted this month gets a call.
New searches: ownership and the first three actions for each.
Rules
Every open job order has a named recruiter and a next step with a date.
If nothing has happened in ten days, the job order is discussed first.
Update statuses before the meeting, not during it.
